nodes.name: Config
nodes.notes: host.docker.internal reaches the FastAPI app when n8n runs in Docker. Use http://localhost:8000 for a native n8n install, or your ngrok URL for n8n Cloud.

nodes.name: Fetch untagged people
nodes.notes: GET /api/people?untagged=true - people from the merged DB that have skills but no skill_category yet. n8n turns the JSON array into one item per person.

parameters.text:
=You are classifying a talent pool for a staffing company.

Person: {{ $json.full_name }}
City: {{ $json.city }}
Skills: {{ $json.skills }}

Assign EXACTLY ONE category:
- "automation-heavy": the skill set centres on workflow automation / AI orchestration tooling (n8n, Zapier, Make, LangChain, LLM pipelines, RPA, scraping used for automation).
- "web-dev": the skill set centres on building web applications (React, JavaScript, front-end, FastAPI/Django as app backends, REST API development).
- "data": the skill set centres on data work (SQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Pandas, ETL, analytics, reporting).
- "generalist": genuinely mixed with no dominant centre of gravity.

Rules:
- Judge the CENTRE OF GRAVITY of the whole set, not the presence of one keyword. "Docker" alone decides nothing.
- Databases used only to back a web app do not make someone "data".
- confidence is your own calibrated probability that a human recruiter would agree, 0-1.
- reason must be one short sentence naming the skills that decided it.

options.systemMessage: You are a precise classifier. Answer only with the requested JSON object.

nodes.name: OpenAI Chat Model
nodes.notes: Swap for Ollama / Groq / Gemini - any chat model node works here. temperature 0 so re-runs are reproducible.

nodes.name: Structured Output Parser
nodes.notes: Forces the model onto the 4-value enum. Without this the LLM invents categories like 'AI/ML' and the API rejects the write-back with a 422.

nodes.name: Confident enough?
nodes.notes: Low-confidence rows are NOT written back - they go to the review branch instead. Silently writing a guess is worse than leaving the field null.

nodes.name: Write category back
nodes.notes: PATCH /api/people/{id}/skill-category - the API re-validates the enum server-side, so a broken flow cannot corrupt the column.

parameters.content:
## What this flow does

1. Pulls people from the merged SQLite DB that have skills but no `skill_category`
2. Sends each one's skill list to an LLM with a 4-value enum
3. Validates the answer (enum + confidence threshold) in code
4. PATCHes the category back into the same `person` row
5. Anything low-confidence or out-of-vocabulary is collected for a human instead of written

The database is reached through the FastAPI app from Task 3 (`app/main.py`), so
n8n never touches the SQLite file directly - two writers on one SQLite file is a
locking problem waiting to happen.
